subject: Dedicated capacity vs VPC — post-demo qualification & sizing questions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@opticore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity vs VPC — post-demo qualification & sizing questions

Alex — thanks for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and the concrete follow-ups we promised so we can finalize a recommended Dedicated configuration (or confirm if Private VPC is necessary):

Recap (short):
- Use case: real-time document summarization + search augmentation in customer support UI.
- Expected production pattern: mix of short chat prompts (avg prompt ~30 tokens) and longer generation for summaries (~input 400 tokens, output 450 tokens).
- Peak TPS target discussed on call: ~18 sustained requests/sec with 3x bursts to ~55 req/sec during high traffic windows.
- Latency goal: 95th <= 250ms for standard prompts; summaries can accept higher p95 up to ~800ms.
- Security: SOC2 and VPC requirement may appear for a subset of customers in Q4.

Primary qualification asks for Dedicated sizing (can you provide these items back to us?):
1) Confirm model family you plan to serve (open model name or LLM family) and whether you expect to run 1 model or a small ensemble (e.g., 1 primary + 1 fallback).
2) Historic token distribution or a 24h sample CSV of requests (timestamps, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens). Attached is a sample CSV we typically use — please replace with your data (opticore-traffic-sample.csv).
3) Desired latency SLOs by workload class (chat vs summary).
4) Any KV/prefix caching expected (e.g., context reuse patterns).
5) Whether you require Private VPC/on-prem for data residency — if yes, we’ll switch the sizing conversation to expected network egress and on-prem hardware constraints.

What we recommend to get to a concrete Dedicated proposal:
- You send the sample traffic CSV and confirm model family + SLOs.
- We run a micro-simulation and propose a GPU mix (e.g., H100-heavy mix vs A100 cost optimized) with estimated slots, throughput, expected P95 latency, and monthly unit cost.

Next steps:
- Please send the sample.csv and any notes on sequence lengths by EOD tomorrow if possible.
- We’ll schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop with Ben (solutions) and Marissa (sales) to walk through the simulation output.

Attachments: opticore-traffic-sample.csv (sample format), redwood-dedicated-sizing-checklist.xlsx (checklist we’ll complete after the workshop).

Thanks — I’ll hold Friday 11am PT for the workshop if that works; otherwise propose a slot.

— Soojin

Soojin — thanks for the clear notes. Attaching a sanitized 24h sample (attached as opticore-traffic-sample.csv). Quick answers inline:

1) Model family: we plan to run an open Llama-3-70B-8k tuned variant (single primary for now, fallback is a smaller 13B).
2) Attached sample included prompt_tokens and completion_tokens. Typical median prompt ~28 tokens, completion median ~320 but summaries push completion to 450–600 tokens.
3) Latency SLOs: chat p95 <= 250ms, long summaries p95 <= 700–800ms (we can queue summaries with higher latency tolerance).
4) KV caching: yes — we expect ~30% of requests to hit cached context (same document reuse within a session).
5) Private VPC: not required on day 1, but likely required for enterprise customers mid-Q4. For now we can evaluate Dedicated hosted in our region (us-west) with an option path to Private VPC later.

We’ll be available Friday 11am PT — please send invite.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs VPC — post-demo qualification & sizing questions

Thanks for the sample and the clarifications, Alex — useful signal. A few technical notes and a preliminary sizing direction based on the sample you shared: 

Preliminary assumptions (from sample):
- Effective average request token footprint: ~350 tokens (prompt+completion) for mixed workload; summaries skew higher.
- Cache hit ~30% reduces effective compute a bit, good to know.

GPU recommendation (tradeoff):
- If low-latency p95 at 250ms for chat is mandatory across 18 sustained TPS, we should be thinking H100-class instances for primary inference — they provide better FP16/FP8 throughput for Llama-3 70B and keep beam/kv costs down. For cost-sensitive staging or early pilot we can start with A100 80GB nodes if you accept slightly lower throughput and tune batching aggressively.

Concurrency & slots: 
- For 18 sustained TPS with 30% cache: effective compute load ≈ 12.6 req/sec. With bursts to 55 req/sec, we plan headroom for ~3x burst capacity.
- For H100, one cluster node (1xH100) can typically sustain ~20–30 mixed-requests/s depending on batch window and max sequence len; recommended starting config: 3 H100 GPUs with autoscale rules (min 2, max 8) to handle typical plus bursts. This gives warm capacity and room for canary/fallback.
- If you want predictable guaranteed throughput, consider Dedicated pool with reserved slots (we’ll map slots to GPU slices in the proposal).

Batching & latency: 
- To hit 250ms p95 we’ll keep batch windows tight for chat (10–20ms), accept longer windows for summaries. We'll enable adaptive batching and prefix KV cache so repeated dialogs are cheap.

Next clarifying asks from our side before a final proposal:
A) Confirm the model quantization you are comfortable with (we recommend int8/4-bit quant for cost but need to validate quality).
B) Provide any hard network egress constraints (for Private VPC planning).
C) Confirm whether fallback to the 13B model is acceptable under heavy load (this lets us design a cheaper burst ladder).

I can sketch cost/throughput curves once we get A, B, C. Happy to run a quick micro-benchmark if you can give us a day to queue a small sample on our side.

— Ben

- Ben: please prepare a 1-page cost/throughput ladder (H100 vs A100) and a draft autoscale policy (min slots, burst headroom) — deliverable for our Friday workshop.
- Marissa: will own scheduling and I’ll send the calendar invite for Friday 11am PT and attach the proposal template and redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf.

Workshop goal: produce a committed Dedicated proposal (recommended GPU mix, predicted sustained TPS, cost estimate, and an optional Private VPC add-on).

I’ve attached our redwood-dedicated-sizing-checklist.xlsx for the meeting — please prefill any missing fields and bring any vendor constraints (e.g., on-prem rack power for Private path).

Thanks — invite will go shortly.
